newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade thin at $66.50-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade thin at $66.50-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday Thursday sold in light volume at $66.00 to $66.50 per cwt, depending on quality, steady to $0.50 per cwt higher than Wednesday's limited sales, feedlot sources said.

About 7,000 head of steers and heifers that should grade select/choice sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area at $66.00 to $66.50. The $66.50 was paid for cattle that would likely yield higher, sources there said.
An estimated 3,000 head sold in Kansas, with steers at $66.50 and lighter-weight heifers at $66.00, Kansas cattle feeders said.
Thursday's sales were viewed by some feedyard sources as residual while packers finish arranging cattle for pickup following Monday's Memorial Day holiday.
Slaughter was seen light on Saturday before the holiday. Major U.S. beef plants will be closed on Monday in observance of Memorial Day.
Several feedlot sources reported selling out their showlists by Thursday. Cattle that were not sold this week were unfinished and could use extra days on feed, they said.
